This page is the interactive version of the lesson notes (PDF). Each section
starts with a problem in a game. Then it explains the idea behind it. It ends
with a **Do it** task and one set of questions. Every question on this page
has its answer: try first, then check.

## Key terms

{{< glossary cross-product surface-normal triangle-mesh winding-order back-face-culling handedness perpendicular dot-product unit-vector forward-vector >}}

## 4.1 Left or right? The cross product in 2D

- A tower must turn to a drone. The dot product says *in front* or
  *behind*, but not *left* or *right*.
- The **cross product** of two 2D vectors is one number:
  f × d = f~x~ d~y~ − f~y~ d~x~.
- **Positive:** d is to the left (turn anticlockwise).
- **Negative:** d is to the right (turn clockwise).
- **Zero:** d is on the same line: straight ahead or straight behind. The dot
  product tells which.
- This works when the y-axis points up.

![f = (2, 1): the cross product with three vectors.](images/cross-sign.png){width=90%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
The order matters: d × f has the opposite sign. Always put the forward
vector first.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Left or right on paper"}
On squared paper, draw f = (2, 1) and the vectors (1, 3), (3, −1) and
(−1, 2) from the same point. Compute f × d for each one. Mark it "left" or
"right" and check with your drawing.

::: {.check}
(2, 1) × (1, 3) = 6 − 1 = 5: left. (2, 1) × (3, −1) = −2 − 3 = −5: right.
(2, 1) × (−1, 2) = 4 + 1 = 5: left.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 1 · Left or right?"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="behind|7"}
A tower faces (1, 0). The drone is in the direction (3, 2). Which way?
:   left

    Why: f × d = 1 × 2 − 0 × 3 = 2: positive, so left.

A tower faces (1, 0). The drone is in the direction (2, −3). Which way?
:   right

    Why: 1 × (−3) − 0 × 2 = −3: negative, so right.

A kart faces (3, 4). The checkpoint is in the direction (4, 3). What is f × d?
:   −7

    Why: 3 × 3 − 4 × 4 = 9 − 16 = −7: the kart must steer right.

A tower faces (1, 0). The drone is in the direction (5, 0). What is f × d?
:   0

    Why: 1 × 0 − 0 × 5 = 0: the drone is on the same line.

f × d = 0 and f · d = 5. What must the tower do?
:   fire straight ahead

    Why: on the same line and in front: straight ahead.
:::
:::

## 4.2 A vector at a right angle to two vectors

- In 3D, the cross product of two vectors is a **vector**:
  a × b = (a~y~ b~z~ − a~z~ b~y~, a~z~ b~x~ − a~x~ b~z~, a~x~ b~y~ − a~y~ b~x~).
- Each part uses the two **other** axes.
- The result is **perpendicular** to a and to b.
- Check every result: its dot product with a and with b must be 0.
- Example: (1, 0, 0) × (0, 1, 0) = (0, 0, 1).

![The three parts of (2, 1, 0) × (0, 3, 1).](images/cross-steps.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Do not multiply matching parts (a~x~ b~x~ …): that is the dot product. The
cross product always mixes two different axes.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The cross product in GeoGebra 3D"}
At geogebra.org/3d, type `u = Vector((2, 1, 0))`, `v = Vector((0, 3, 1))`
and `w = Cross(u, v)`. Turn the view. Then type `w * u` and `w * v`. What
are the two dot products?

::: {.check}
w = (1, −2, 6). Both dot products are 0: w is at a right angle to u and to v.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 2 · Compute it"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 3, 0)|(0, 0, −1)|a number"}
(1, 0, 0) × (0, 1, 0)
:   (0, 0, 1)

    Why: the x-axis × the y-axis gives the z-axis.

(2, 1, 0) × (0, 3, 1)
:   (1, −2, 6)

    Why: x: 1 × 1 − 0 × 3 = 1; y: 0 × 0 − 2 × 1 = −2; z: 2 × 3 − 1 × 0 = 6.

(0, 1, 0) × (0, 0, 1)
:   (1, 0, 0)

    Why: x: 1 × 1 − 0 × 0 = 1; the y and z parts are 0.

What kind of result does the 3D cross product give?
:   a vector

    Why: three parts: a vector at a right angle to both.

(1, −2, 6) · (2, 1, 0) = 0. What does this check show?
:   the result is perpendicular to (2, 1, 0)

    Why: a dot product of 0 means a right angle.
:::
:::

## 4.3 Which way does it point? The order and the hand rule

- Two vectors on a floor have two directions at a right angle: up and down.
- The **order** decides: b × a = −(a × b).
- **Curl rule:** fingers along a, curl them towards b, the thumb shows
  a × b.
- Use the hand of the tool: the **left** hand in Unity, the **right** hand
  in GeoGebra and Blender. The numbers are the same.
- Two vectors on one line give the zero vector.

![Swapping the order turns the result around (Unity axes: left hand).](images/curl-rule.png){width=88%}

{{< sim file="sims/normal-lab.html" poster="sims/normal-lab.png" title="Normal Lab: the normal of a triangle" height="720" >}}

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · The curl rule in Normal Lab"}
In **Normal Lab** (Unity axes), curl the fingers of your left hand from the
purple edge (0, 0, 2) to the blue edge (2, 0, 0). Where does your thumb
point? Compare with the green arrow. Press **Swap B and C** and do it again.

::: {.check}
Before the swap the thumb and the green arrow point up: n = (0, 4, 0). After
the swap they point down: n = (0, −4, 0).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 3 · Order and hand"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(2, 1, 4)|the right hand"}
a × b = (2, −1, 4). What is b × a?
:   (−2, 1, −4)

    Why: swapping the order turns the result around: every sign changes.

A ship flies forward f = (0, 0, 1). Its right wing is r = (1, 0, 0). What is f × r?
:   (0, 1, 0)

    Why: y-part: 1 × 1 − 0 × 0 = 1; the other parts are 0: up.

Which hand do you use for the curl rule in Unity?
:   the left hand

    Why: Unity is left-handed.

(1, 2, 0) × (2, 4, 0). What is the result?
:   (0, 0, 0)

    Why: every part is 0, for example z: 1 × 4 − 2 × 2 = 0.

Why is (1, 2, 0) × (2, 4, 0) the zero vector?
:   the two vectors lie on one line

    Why: (2, 4, 0) = 2 × (1, 2, 0): no single direction is at a right angle to both.
:::
:::

## 4.4 Which way does a surface face? The normal of a triangle

- A 3D model is a **triangle mesh**: many small, flat triangles.
- The **normal** is a unit vector at a right angle to the surface. It points
  out of the front side.
- For a triangle A, B, C: n = (B − A) × (C − A), then normalize.
- The **winding order** (the order of the corners) decides the front.
  A, C, B turns the normal around.
- Floor A = (0, 0, 0), B = (0, 0, 2), C = (2, 0, 0): n = (0, 4, 0), unit
  normal (0, 1, 0): up.
- Lift C to (2, 2, 0): n = (−4, 4, 0). The normal leans to the side.

![The same triangle with two winding orders.](images/normal.png){width=88%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
Use the **edges** B − A and C − A, not the corners B and C.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Lift the corner"}
In **Normal Lab**, move **height of C** to 1, then to 2. Each time, write
the second edge C − A and the normal n. Check one normal on paper.

::: {.check}
Height 1: C − A = (2, 1, 0), n = (−2, 4, 0). Height 2: C − A = (2, 2, 0),
n = (−4, 4, 0). The higher the corner, the more the normal leans.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 4 · Normals"}
Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(0, 0, 2)|(4, 0, 0)"}
A = (0, 0, 0), B = (0, 0, 2), C = (2, 0, 0). What is n = (B − A) × (C − A)?
:   (0, 4, 0)

    Why: (0, 0, 2) × (2, 0, 0): y-part 2 × 2 − 0 × 0 = 4.

The same triangle listed as A, C, B. What is n?
:   (0, −4, 0)

    Why: the other winding order turns the normal around.

A = (0, 0, 0), B = (0, 0, 3), C = (3, 0, 0). Which way does the triangle face?
:   up

    Why: n = (0, 9, 0): the y-part is positive, so up.

What decides the front side of a triangle?
:   the winding order

    Why: A, B, C and A, C, B give opposite normals.

n = (0, 4, 0). What is the unit normal?
:   (0, 1, 0)

    Why: divide by its length 4.
:::
:::

## 4.5 Facing the camera: back-face culling

- The normal tells which side of a triangle the camera sees. It uses the
  dot product (Lecture 3).
- v goes from the triangle to the camera.
- n · v > 0: the camera sees the front, the game draws the triangle.
- n · v < 0: the camera sees the back, the game skips it. This is
  **back-face culling**: the hidden back of a model is not drawn.

![The camera above sees the front; the camera below sees the back.](images/culling.png){width=46%}

::: {.callout-warning title="Watch out!"}
A wrong winding order makes a normal point inwards. The game skips the
triangle, and the player sees a hole in the model.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Do it · Look from below"}
In **Normal Lab**, press **View from below**, then **View from above**. Read
the message each time. What happens to the green triangle, and why?

::: {.check}
From below: "back", and the triangle is not drawn. From above: "front", and
it is drawn. The camera below sees the back side (n · v < 0).
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 5 · Draw it or skip it?"}
A floor triangle at P = (1, 0, 1) has n = (0, 1, 0). Choose the right
answer.

::: {.match extra="draw it, n · v = −3|the camera is too far"}
The camera is at (1, 5, −4), so v = (0, 5, −5). What does the game do?
:   draw it, n · v = 5

    Why: (0, 1, 0) · (0, 5, −5) = 5: positive, the front is seen.

The camera is at (1, −3, 1), so v = (0, −3, 0). What does the game do?
:   skip it, n · v = −3

    Why: negative: the camera is under the floor and sees its back.

Why does a game skip back faces?
:   they are hidden, so it saves work

    Why: the back of a closed model is never seen.

A model was made with the wrong winding order. What does the player see?
:   holes in the model

    Why: its normals point inwards, so the game skips faces that should be seen.
:::
:::

## Game challenge: Turret Turn {.challenge}

Work alone. Use every section of today.

**Turret Turn** is a tower-defence game. The tower stands at T = (4, 4) and
looks along f = (1, 0). Four drones fly in: A at (7, 6), B at (6, 1), C at
(1, 4) and D at (9, 4). For each drone the tower must turn left, turn right,
fire straight ahead or turn around. Later the tower looks up: f = (0, 1).

{{< sim file="sims/turret-turn.html" poster="sims/turret-turn.png" title="Turret Turn: left, right, fire or turn around" kind="game" height="700" >}}

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 6 · The tower looks right"}
Turret Turn: T = (4, 4), f = (1, 0). Drones A (7, 6), B (6, 1), C (1, 4),
D (9, 4). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="(3, −2)|turn right"}
The vector d from the tower to drone A.
:   (3, 2)

    Why: A − T = (7 − 4, 6 − 4).

f × d for drone B, with d = (2, −3).
:   −3

    Why: 1 × (−3) − 0 × 2 = −3: turn right.

What must the tower do for drone C, with d = (−3, 0)?
:   turn around

    Why: f × d = 0 and f · d = −3: on the line, behind.

What must the tower do for drone D, with d = (5, 0)?
:   fire straight ahead

    Why: f × d = 0 and f · d = 5: on the line, in front.
:::
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it 7 · The tower looks up (harder)"}
Turret Turn: T = (4, 4), now f = (0, 1). Drone A (7, 6), drone E (2, 7),
drone F (4, 8). Choose the right answer.

::: {.match extra="2|turn around"}
f × d for drone A, with d = (3, 2).
:   −3

    Why: (0, 1) × (3, 2) = 0 × 2 − 1 × 3 = −3.

What must the tower do for drone A now?
:   turn right

    Why: f × d = −3 is negative.

What must the tower do for drone E, with d = (−2, 3)?
:   turn left

    Why: (0, 1) × (−2, 3) = 0 × 3 − 1 × (−2) = 2: positive.

What must the tower do for drone F, with d = (0, 4)?
:   fire straight ahead

    Why: f × d = 0 and f · d = 4: straight ahead.

The tower's right is (1, 0) and its forward is (0, 1). In 3D, (1, 0, 0) × (0, 1, 0) is…
:   (0, 0, 1)

    Why: the x-axis × the y-axis gives the z-axis.
:::
:::

## Summary {.summary}

- 2D: f × d = f~x~ d~y~ − f~y~ d~x~. Positive: left. Negative: right. Zero: on the same line.
- 3D: a × b is a vector at a right angle to a and b. Check it with two dot products.
- The order matters: b × a = −(a × b). Curl rule: left hand in Unity.
- Triangle normal: n = (B − A) × (C − A), normalized. The winding order decides the front.
- n · v < 0: the camera sees the back face, and the game skips it.
